title: The Pond Concert Promise
story:
Ada wanted to invite Mira to Frog’s pond concert, and Ben wanted to help. Yet Mira wanted quiet while a breeze skimmed the pond, and Ada’s wide lily pad still waited in the garden. Frog’s acorn drum waited too, although it belonged to Frog and not to Ada.

Ada peeked toward Mira’s porch and noticed Mira sitting with a book, enjoying quiet. “Quiet,” Ada whispered, “is Mira’s wish today.”

Ada picked up the painted invitation and carried it from the garden to the porch. She held it carefully; the blue frog on its front had very important-looking spots.

Ada told Frog, “Mira wants quiet today.” Frog nodded. “Then my drum shall use its teeny-tiniest toes.”

With the invitation waiting on the porch, Ada walked up from the garden. She practiced her polite knock, then decided one knock was plenty.

Frog carried his acorn drum from the garden to the pond. He set it near the water, where its round wooden belly was ready to go bonk—or perhaps merely bonk politely.

Knowing Mira wanted quiet, Frog played a gentle song on the acorn drum. Tap, hush, tap—each note skimmed the pond like a tiny pebble that had learned manners.

Mira smiled and listened to Frog’s gentle pond song. She stayed on the porch, quiet as a sleeping feather, while the soft taps reached her.

Ada gave Mira the painted invitation. “A pond concert,” she said, “with a very small volume knob.” Mira accepted it from Ada with a curious smile.

The invitation was safely delivered: Mira now owned the painted card, and Ada’s delivery was complete. The blue frog on the card seemed pleased with its new address.

Mira smiled and listened as Frog’s gentle notes floated across the still pond. Ada’s invitation rested safely in Mira’s hands, and the acorn drum made no thunder at all. In the evening light, each quiet ripple looked like a little silver ear, listening too.

title: The Pond Concert Promise
story:
Ada hoped to invite Mira to Frog’s pond concert, and Ben hoped to help. Mira wanted to join, but a breeze teased the pond and the wide lily pad was still in the garden. Frog’s drum waited there too, stubbornly refusing to teleport.

Ada picked up the painted invitation and carried it from the garden to the porch. She held it carefully; the blue frog on its front had very important-looking spots.

Ada watched Mira on the porch, where Mira leaned forward as though eager for music. “She wants to join,” Ada observed. “That is wonderfully less quiet than a potato.” Ada pushed her wide lily pad from the garden onto the pond. It floated broad and steady, making a perfect little platform for Frog’s planned rhythm. Ada told Frog that Mira wanted to join the concert. Frog puffed up happily. “Excellent! I know three rhythms and one accidental sneeze.”

With the invitation waiting on the porch, Ada walked up from the garden. She practiced her polite knock, then decided one knock was plenty.

Ada gave Mira the painted invitation. “You’re invited to join Frog’s concert,” Ada said. Mira accepted the card, already listening for the next beat.

Frog noticed a breeze ruffling the pond. “The water is tickling the reeds,” he said. “A lily pad might go sailing without buying a ticket.”

The invitation was safely delivered: Mira now owned the painted card, and Ada’s delivery was complete. The blue frog on the card seemed pleased with its new address.

Frog told Ada about the breezy pond. Ada looked at the waving reeds and nodded. “Then we’ll give my lily pad something sturdy to hold.”

Ada and Ben anchored the lily pad against the breeze. Ben held the cord while Ada pressed the anchor down; the pad stopped drifting and stayed put.

With the lily pad anchored against the breeze, Frog turned it into a lively rhythm. His drumbeat and the pad’s gentle thump made a bouncy, dependable pulse.

Mira joined the lively pond rhythm from the porch, tapping along with her fingers. Her smile arrived on the beat, though her left thumb was slightly ahead of everyone.

Mira joined the lively rhythm as Frog played his anchored lily-pad beat. The breeze whisked over the water, but the pad stayed steady, and Ada’s invitation remained safely with Mira. Sunlight flashed on the ripples while Ben grinned beside the anchor, right on the beat.

title: The Pond Concert Promise

Ada told Frog, “Mira wants quiet today.” Frog nodded. “Then my drum shall use its teeny-tiniest toes.”

Knowing Mira wanted quiet, Frog played a gentle song on the acorn drum. Tap, hush, tap—each note skimmed the pond like a tiny pebble that had learned manners.

title: The Pond Concert Promise
story:

title: The Pond Concert Promise
story:
Ada wanted to invite Mira to Frog’s pond concert, and Ben wanted to help. But the pond was still, Mira wanted quiet, and nobody yet knew what sort of concert would fit. The painted invitation waited in Ada’s garden beside Frog’s drum.

Ada picked up the painted invitation and carried it from the garden to the porch. She held it carefully; the blue frog on its front had very important-looking spots.

With the invitation waiting on the porch, Ada walked up from the garden. She practiced her polite knock, then decided one knock was plenty.

Ada peeked toward Mira’s porch and noticed Mira sitting with a book, enjoying quiet. “Quiet,” Ada whispered, “is Mira’s wish today.” Ada told Frog, “Mira wants quiet today.” Frog nodded. “Then my drum shall use its teeny-tiniest toes.”

Ada gave Mira the painted invitation. “A pond concert,” she said, “with a very small volume knob.” Mira accepted it from Ada with a curious smile.

The invitation was safely delivered: Mira now owned the painted card, and Ada’s delivery was complete. The blue frog on the card seemed pleased with its new address.

Frog carried his acorn drum from the garden to the pond. He set it near the water, where its round wooden belly was ready to go bonk—or perhaps merely bonk politely.

Knowing Mira wanted quiet, Frog played a gentle song on the acorn drum. Tap, hush, tap—each note skimmed the pond like a tiny pebble that had learned manners.

Mira smiled and listened to Frog’s gentle pond song. She stayed on the porch, quiet as a sleeping feather, while the soft taps reached her.

Mira smiled and listened as Frog’s gentle notes floated across the still pond. Ada’s invitation rested safely in Mira’s hands, and the acorn drum made no thunder at all. In the evening light, each quiet ripple looked like a little silver ear, listening too.

title: The Pond Concert Promise
story:
Ada planned to invite Mira to Frog’s pond concert, while Ben hoped to help. Mira wanted to join, but the pond was perfectly still and the concert tools were scattered in the garden. Ada’s painted invitation waited beside a wide lily pad, as if both were awaiting instructions.

Ada watched Mira on the porch, where Mira leaned forward as though eager for music. “She wants to join,” Ada observed. “That is wonderfully less quiet than a potato.”

Ada picked up the painted invitation and carried it from the garden to the porch. She held it carefully; the blue frog on its front had very important-looking spots.

Ada told Frog that Mira wanted to join the concert. Frog puffed up happily. “Excellent! I know three rhythms and one accidental sneeze.” Ada pushed her wide lily pad from the garden onto the pond. It floated broad and steady, making a perfect little platform for Frog’s planned rhythm.

With the invitation waiting on the porch, Ada walked up from the garden. She practiced her polite knock, then decided one knock was plenty.

Ada gave Mira the painted invitation. “You’re invited to join Frog’s concert,” Ada said. Mira accepted the card, already listening for the next beat.

The invitation was safely delivered: Mira now owned the painted card, and Ada’s delivery was complete. The blue frog on the card seemed pleased with its new address.

Frog began a lively rhythm on the lily pad. The still pond let every plip and plop travel outward, while the pad bobbed like a cheerful green drumhead.

Mira joined the lively pond rhythm from the porch, tapping along with her fingers. Her smile arrived on the beat, though her left thumb was slightly ahead of everyone.

Mira joined Frog’s lively rhythm while Ada watched from the porch, and the invitation stayed safely with its new owner. The still pond carried the music in bright circles; even the lily pad seemed to bounce, as if it had swallowed a very polite trampoline.

title: The Pond Concert Promise
story:
Ada hoped to invite Mira to Frog’s pond concert, and Ben hoped to help. Mira wanted to join, but a breeze teased the pond and the wide lily pad was still in the garden. Frog’s drum waited there too, stubbornly refusing to teleport.

Ada picked up the painted invitation and carried it from the garden to the porch. She held it carefully; the blue frog on its front had very important-looking spots.

Frog noticed a breeze ruffling the pond. “The water is tickling the reeds,” he said. “A lily pad might go sailing without buying a ticket.” Ada watched Mira on the porch, where Mira leaned forward as though eager for music. “She wants to join,” Ada observed. “That is wonderfully less quiet than a potato.” Frog told Ada about the breezy pond. Ada looked at the waving reeds and nodded. “Then we’ll give my lily pad something sturdy to hold.” Ada told Frog that Mira wanted to join the concert. Frog puffed up happily. “Excellent! I know three rhythms and one accidental sneeze.” Ada pushed her wide lily pad from the garden onto the pond. It floated broad and steady, making a perfect little platform for Frog’s planned rhythm.

Ada and Ben anchored the lily pad against the breeze. Ben held the cord while Ada pressed the anchor down; the pad stopped drifting and stayed put.

With the lily pad anchored against the breeze, Frog turned it into a lively rhythm. His drumbeat and the pad’s gentle thump made a bouncy, dependable pulse.

With the invitation waiting on the porch, Ada walked up from the garden. She practiced her polite knock, then decided one knock was plenty.

Ada gave Mira the painted invitation. “You’re invited to join Frog’s concert,” Ada said. Mira accepted the card, already listening for the next beat.

Mira joined the lively pond rhythm from the porch, tapping along with her fingers. Her smile arrived on the beat, though her left thumb was slightly ahead of everyone.

The invitation was safely delivered: Mira now owned the painted card, and Ada’s delivery was complete. The blue frog on the card seemed pleased with its new address.

Mira joined the lively rhythm as Frog played his anchored lily-pad beat. The breeze whisked over the water, but the pad stayed steady, and Ada’s invitation remained safely with Mira. Sunlight flashed on the ripples while Ben grinned beside the anchor, right on the beat.

Ada planned to invite Mira to Frog’s pond concert, while Ben hoped to help. Mira wanted to join, but the pond was perfectly still and the concert tools were scattered in the garden. Ada’s painted invitation waited beside a wide lily pad, as if both were awaiting instructions.

Ada pushed her wide lily pad from the garden onto the pond. It floated broad and steady, making a perfect little platform for Frog’s planned rhythm. Ada watched Mira on the porch, where Mira leaned forward as though eager for music. “She wants to join,” Ada observed. “That is wonderfully less quiet than a potato.”

Ada picked up the painted invitation and carried it from the garden to the porch. She held it carefully; the blue frog on its front had very important-looking spots.

Ada told Frog that Mira wanted to join the concert. Frog puffed up happily. “Excellent! I know three rhythms and one accidental sneeze.”

Frog began a lively rhythm on the lily pad. The still pond let every plip and plop travel outward, while the pad bobbed like a cheerful green drumhead.

With the invitation waiting on the porch, Ada walked up from the garden. She practiced her polite knock, then decided one knock was plenty.

Mira joined the lively pond rhythm from the porch, tapping along with her fingers. Her smile arrived on the beat, though her left thumb was slightly ahead of everyone.

Ada gave Mira the painted invitation. “You’re invited to join Frog’s concert,” Ada said. Mira accepted the card, already listening for the next beat.

The invitation was safely delivered: Mira now owned the painted card, and Ada’s delivery was complete. The blue frog on the card seemed pleased with its new address.

Mira joined Frog’s lively rhythm while Ada watched from the porch, and the invitation stayed safely with its new owner. The still pond carried the music in bright circles; even the lily pad seemed to bounce, as if it had swallowed a very polite trampoline.

title: The Pond Concert Promise
story:
Ada wanted to invite Mira to Frog’s pond concert, and Ben wanted to help. But the pond was still, Mira wanted quiet, and nobody yet knew what sort of concert would fit. The painted invitation waited in Ada’s garden beside Frog’s drum.

Ada peeked toward Mira’s porch and noticed Mira sitting with a book, enjoying quiet. “Quiet,” Ada whispered, “is Mira’s wish today.”

Ada picked up the painted invitation and carried it from the garden to the porch. She held it carefully; the blue frog on its front had very important-looking spots.

With the invitation waiting on the porch, Ada walked up from the garden. She practiced her polite knock, then decided one knock was plenty.

Ada gave Mira the painted invitation. “A pond concert,” she said, “with a very small volume knob.” Mira accepted it from Ada with a curious smile.

The invitation was safely delivered: Mira now owned the painted card, and Ada’s delivery was complete. The blue frog on the card seemed pleased with its new address.

Frog carried his acorn drum from the garden to the pond. He set it near the water, where its round wooden belly was ready to go bonk—or perhaps merely bonk politely. Ada told Frog, “Mira wants quiet today.” Frog nodded. “Then my drum shall use its teeny-tiniest toes.”

Knowing Mira wanted quiet, Frog played a gentle song on the acorn drum. Tap, hush, tap—each note skimmed the pond like a tiny pebble that had learned manners.

Mira smiled and listened to Frog’s gentle pond song. She stayed on the porch, quiet as a sleeping feather, while the soft taps reached her.

Mira smiled and listened as Frog’s gentle notes floated across the still pond. Ada’s invitation rested safely in Mira’s hands, and the acorn drum made no thunder at all. In the evening light, each quiet ripple looked like a little silver ear, listening too.

title: The Pond Concert Promise
story:
Ada hoped to invite Mira to Frog’s pond concert, and Ben hoped to help. Mira wanted to join, but a breeze teased the pond and the wide lily pad was still in the garden. Frog’s drum waited there too, stubbornly refusing to teleport.

Ada pushed her wide lily pad from the garden onto the pond. It floated broad and steady, making a perfect little platform for Frog’s planned rhythm.

Ada picked up the painted invitation and carried it from the garden to the porch. She held it carefully; the blue frog on its front had very important-looking spots.

Ada watched Mira on the porch, where Mira leaned forward as though eager for music. “She wants to join,” Ada observed. “That is wonderfully less quiet than a potato.”

With the invitation waiting on the porch, Ada walked up from the garden. She practiced her polite knock, then decided one knock was plenty.

Frog noticed a breeze ruffling the pond. “The water is tickling the reeds,” he said. “A lily pad might go sailing without buying a ticket.” Frog told Ada about the breezy pond. Ada looked at the waving reeds and nodded. “Then we’ll give my lily pad something sturdy to hold.”

Ada gave Mira the painted invitation. “You’re invited to join Frog’s concert,” Ada said. Mira accepted the card, already listening for the next beat.

The invitation was safely delivered: Mira now owned the painted card, and Ada’s delivery was complete. The blue frog on the card seemed pleased with its new address.

Ada and Ben anchored the lily pad against the breeze. Ben held the cord while Ada pressed the anchor down; the pad stopped drifting and stayed put.

Ada told Frog that Mira wanted to join the concert. Frog puffed up happily. “Excellent! I know three rhythms and one accidental sneeze.”

With the lily pad anchored against the breeze, Frog turned it into a lively rhythm. His drumbeat and the pad’s gentle thump made a bouncy, dependable pulse.

Mira joined the lively pond rhythm from the porch, tapping along with her fingers. Her smile arrived on the beat, though her left thumb was slightly ahead of everyone.

Mira joined the lively rhythm as Frog played his anchored lily-pad beat. The breeze whisked over the water, but the pad stayed steady, and Ada’s invitation remained safely with Mira. Sunlight flashed on the ripples while Ben grinned beside the anchor, right on the beat.

title: The Pond Concert Promise
story:
Ada hoped to invite Mira to Frog’s pond concert, and Ben hoped to help. Mira wanted to join, but a breeze teased the pond and the wide lily pad was still in the garden. Frog’s drum waited there too, stubbornly refusing to teleport.

Ada picked up the painted invitation and carried it from the garden to the porch. She held it carefully; the blue frog on its front had very important-looking spots.

Frog noticed a breeze ruffling the pond. “The water is tickling the reeds,” he said. “A lily pad might go sailing without buying a ticket.” Ada pushed her wide lily pad from the garden onto the pond. It floated broad and steady, making a perfect little platform for Frog’s planned rhythm. Frog told Ada about the breezy pond. Ada looked at the waving reeds and nodded. “Then we’ll give my lily pad something sturdy to hold.” Ada watched Mira on the porch, where Mira leaned forward as though eager for music. “She wants to join,” Ada observed. “That is wonderfully less quiet than a potato.” Ada told Frog that Mira wanted to join the concert. Frog puffed up happily. “Excellent! I know three rhythms and one accidental sneeze.”

Ada and Ben anchored the lily pad against the breeze. Ben held the cord while Ada pressed the anchor down; the pad stopped drifting and stayed put.

With the invitation waiting on the porch, Ada walked up from the garden. She practiced her polite knock, then decided one knock was plenty.

With the lily pad anchored against the breeze, Frog turned it into a lively rhythm. His drumbeat and the pad’s gentle thump made a bouncy, dependable pulse.

Ada gave Mira the painted invitation. “You’re invited to join Frog’s concert,” Ada said. Mira accepted the card, already listening for the next beat.

Mira joined the lively pond rhythm from the porch, tapping along with her fingers. Her smile arrived on the beat, though her left thumb was slightly ahead of everyone.

The invitation was safely delivered: Mira now owned the painted card, and Ada’s delivery was complete. The blue frog on the card seemed pleased with its new address.

Mira joined the lively rhythm as Frog played his anchored lily-pad beat. The breeze whisked over the water, but the pad stayed steady, and Ada’s invitation remained safely with Mira. Sunlight flashed on the ripples while Ben grinned beside the anchor, right on the beat.

title: The Pond Concert Promise

Ada picked up the painted invitation and carried it from the garden to the porch. She held it carefully; the blue frog on its front had very important-looking spots.

With the invitation waiting on the porch, Ada walked up from the garden. She practiced her polite knock, then decided one knock was plenty.

Ada gave Mira the painted invitation. “A pond concert,” she said, “with a very small volume knob.” Mira accepted it from Ada with a curious smile.

The invitation was safely delivered: Mira now owned the painted card, and Ada’s delivery was complete. The blue frog on the card seemed pleased with its new address.

Ada told Frog, “Mira wants quiet today.” Frog nodded. “Then my drum shall use its teeny-tiniest toes.”

Knowing Mira wanted quiet, Frog played a gentle song on the acorn drum. Tap, hush, tap—each note skimmed the pond like a tiny pebble that had learned manners.

Mira smiled and listened to Frog’s gentle pond song. She stayed on the porch, quiet as a sleeping feather, while the soft taps reached her.

Mira smiled and listened as Frog’s gentle notes floated across the still pond. Ada’s invitation rested safely in Mira’s hands, and the acorn drum made no thunder at all. In the evening light, each quiet ripple looked like a little silver ear, listening too.

title: The Pond Concert Promise
story:

title: The Pond Concert Promise
story:
Ada hoped to invite Mira to Frog’s pond concert, and Ben hoped to help. Mira wanted to join, but a breeze teased the pond and the wide lily pad was still in the garden. Frog’s drum waited there too, stubbornly refusing to teleport.

Ada picked up the painted invitation and carried it from the garden to the porch. She held it carefully; the blue frog on its front had very important-looking spots.

Frog noticed a breeze ruffling the pond. “The water is tickling the reeds,” he said. “A lily pad might go sailing without buying a ticket.” Ada watched Mira on the porch, where Mira leaned forward as though eager for music. “She wants to join,” Ada observed. “That is wonderfully less quiet than a potato.” Frog told Ada about the breezy pond. Ada looked at the waving reeds and nodded. “Then we’ll give my lily pad something sturdy to hold.” Ada told Frog that Mira wanted to join the concert. Frog puffed up happily. “Excellent! I know three rhythms and one accidental sneeze.” Ada pushed her wide lily pad from the garden onto the pond. It floated broad and steady, making a perfect little platform for Frog’s planned rhythm.

With the invitation waiting on the porch, Ada walked up from the garden. She practiced her polite knock, then decided one knock was plenty.

Ada gave Mira the painted invitation. “You’re invited to join Frog’s concert,” Ada said. Mira accepted the card, already listening for the next beat.

Ada and Ben anchored the lily pad against the breeze. Ben held the cord while Ada pressed the anchor down; the pad stopped drifting and stayed put.

The invitation was safely delivered: Mira now owned the painted card, and Ada’s delivery was complete. The blue frog on the card seemed pleased with its new address.

With the lily pad anchored against the breeze, Frog turned it into a lively rhythm. His drumbeat and the pad’s gentle thump made a bouncy, dependable pulse.

Mira joined the lively pond rhythm from the porch, tapping along with her fingers. Her smile arrived on the beat, though her left thumb was slightly ahead of everyone.

Mira joined the lively rhythm as Frog played his anchored lily-pad beat. The breeze whisked over the water, but the pad stayed steady, and Ada’s invitation remained safely with Mira. Sunlight flashed on the ripples while Ben grinned beside the anchor, right on the beat.

title: The Pond Concert Promise

Ada looked at the waving reeds and nodded. “Then we’ll give my lily pad something sturdy to hold.”

Knowing Mira wanted quiet, Frog played a gentle song on the acorn drum. Tap, hush, tap—each note skimmed the pond like a tiny pebble that had learned manners.

Mira smiled and listened to Frog’s gentle pond song. She stayed on the porch, quiet as a sleeping feather, while the soft taps reached her.

Ada and Ben anchored the lily pad against the breeze. Ben held the cord while Ada pressed the anchor down; the pad stopped drifting and stayed put.

Ada picked up the painted invitation and carried it from the garden to the porch. She held it carefully; the blue frog on its front had very important-looking spots.

With the invitation waiting on the porch, Ada walked up from the garden. She practiced her polite knock, then decided one knock was plenty.

Ada gave Mira the painted invitation. “A pond concert,” she said, “with a very small volume knob.” Mira accepted it from Ada with a curious smile.

The invitation was safely delivered: Mira now owned the painted card, and Ada’s delivery was complete. The blue frog on the card seemed pleased with its new address.

Mira smiled and listened to Frog’s gentle song while the anchored lily pad held steady in the breezy pond. Ben’s helping hands had made a difference, and Ada’s invitation rested with Mira. Across the water, soft notes trembled like tiny lanterns tied safely to their strings.

title: The Pond Concert Promise
story:
Ada hoped to invite Mira to Frog’s pond concert, and Ben hoped to help. Mira wanted to join, but a breeze teased the pond and the wide lily pad was still in the garden. Frog’s drum waited there too, stubbornly refusing to teleport.

Frog noticed a breeze ruffling the pond. “The water is tickling the reeds,” he said. “A lily pad might go sailing without buying a ticket.” Ada watched Mira on the porch, where Mira leaned forward as though eager for music. “She wants to join,” Ada observed. “That is wonderfully less quiet than a potato.” Frog told Ada about the breezy pond. Ada looked at the waving reeds and nodded. “Then we’ll give my lily pad something sturdy to hold.” Ada told Frog that Mira wanted to join the concert. Frog puffed up happily. “Excellent! I know three rhythms and one accidental sneeze.” Ada pushed her wide lily pad from the garden onto the pond. It floated broad and steady, making a perfect little platform for Frog’s planned rhythm.

Ada and Ben anchored the lily pad against the breeze. Ben held the cord while Ada pressed the anchor down; the pad stopped drifting and stayed put.

With the lily pad anchored against the breeze, Frog turned it into a lively rhythm. His drumbeat and the pad’s gentle thump made a bouncy, dependable pulse.

Ada picked up the painted invitation and carried it from the garden to the porch. She held it carefully; the blue frog on its front had very important-looking spots.

With the invitation waiting on the porch, Ada walked up from the garden. She practiced her polite knock, then decided one knock was plenty.

Mira joined the lively pond rhythm from the porch, tapping along with her fingers. Her smile arrived on the beat, though her left thumb was slightly ahead of everyone.

Ada gave Mira the painted invitation. “You’re invited to join Frog’s concert,” Ada said. Mira accepted the card, already listening for the next beat.

The invitation was safely delivered: Mira now owned the painted card, and Ada’s delivery was complete. The blue frog on the card seemed pleased with its new address.

Mira joined the lively rhythm as Frog played his anchored lily-pad beat. The breeze whisked over the water, but the pad stayed steady, and Ada’s invitation remained safely with Mira. Sunlight flashed on the ripples while Ben grinned beside the anchor, right on the beat.

title: The Pond Concert Promise
story:

Mira smiled and listened to Frog’s gentle pond song. She stayed on the porch, quiet as a sleeping feather, while the soft taps reached her.

The invitation was safely delivered: Mira now owned the painted card, and Ada’s delivery was complete. The blue frog on the card seemed pleased with its new address.

Mira smiled and listened as Frog’s gentle notes floated across the still pond. Ada’s invitation rested safely in Mira’s hands, and the acorn drum made no thunder at all. In the evening light, each quiet ripple looked like a little silver ear, listening too.

title: The Pond Concert Promise
story:
Ada hoped to invite Mira to Frog’s pond concert, and Ben hoped to help. Mira wanted to join, but a breeze teased the pond and the wide lily pad was still in the garden. Frog’s drum waited there too, stubbornly refusing to teleport.

Ada picked up the painted invitation and carried it from the garden to the porch. She held it carefully; the blue frog on its front had very important-looking spots.

Ada watched Mira on the porch, where Mira leaned forward as though eager for music. “She wants to join,” Ada observed. “That is wonderfully less quiet than a potato.” Ada told Frog that Mira wanted to join the concert. Frog puffed up happily. “Excellent! I know three rhythms and one accidental sneeze.” Frog noticed a breeze ruffling the pond. “The water is tickling the reeds,” he said. “A lily pad might go sailing without buying a ticket.” Ada pushed her wide lily pad from the garden onto the pond. It floated broad and steady, making a perfect little platform for Frog’s planned rhythm.

With the invitation waiting on the porch, Ada walked up from the garden. She practiced her polite knock, then decided one knock was plenty.

Frog told Ada about the breezy pond. Ada looked at the waving reeds and nodded. “Then we’ll give my lily pad something sturdy to hold.”

Ada and Ben anchored the lily pad against the breeze. Ben held the cord while Ada pressed the anchor down; the pad stopped drifting and stayed put.

With the lily pad anchored against the breeze, Frog turned it into a lively rhythm. His drumbeat and the pad’s gentle thump made a bouncy, dependable pulse.

Mira joined the lively pond rhythm from the porch, tapping along with her fingers. Her smile arrived on the beat, though her left thumb was slightly ahead of everyone.

Ada gave Mira the painted invitation. “You’re invited to join Frog’s concert,” Ada said. Mira accepted the card, already listening for the next beat.

The invitation was safely delivered: Mira now owned the painted card, and Ada’s delivery was complete. The blue frog on the card seemed pleased with its new address.

Mira joined the lively rhythm as Frog played his anchored lily-pad beat. The breeze whisked over the water, but the pad stayed steady, and Ada’s invitation remained safely with Mira. Sunlight flashed on the ripples while Ben grinned beside the anchor, right on the beat.

title: The Pond Concert Promise
story:
Ada planned to invite Mira to Frog’s pond concert, while Ben hoped to help. Mira wanted to join, but the pond was perfectly still and the concert tools were scattered in the garden. Ada’s painted invitation waited beside a wide lily pad, as if both were awaiting instructions.

Ada watched Mira on the porch, where Mira leaned forward as though eager for music. “She wants to join,” Ada observed. “That is wonderfully less quiet than a potato.” Ada told Frog that Mira wanted to join the concert. Frog puffed up happily. “Excellent! I know three rhythms and one accidental sneeze.” Ada pushed her wide lily pad from the garden onto the pond. It floated broad and steady, making a perfect little platform for Frog’s planned rhythm.

Ada picked up the painted invitation and carried it from the garden to the porch. She held it carefully; the blue frog on its front had very important-looking spots.

With the invitation waiting on the porch, Ada walked up from the garden. She practiced her polite knock, then decided one knock was plenty.

Frog began a lively rhythm on the lily pad. The still pond let every plip and plop travel outward, while the pad bobbed like a cheerful green drumhead.

Ada gave Mira the painted invitation. “You’re invited to join Frog’s concert,” Ada said. Mira accepted the card, already listening for the next beat.

Mira joined the lively pond rhythm from the porch, tapping along with her fingers. Her smile arrived on the beat, though her left thumb was slightly ahead of everyone.

The invitation was safely delivered: Mira now owned the painted card, and Ada’s delivery was complete. The blue frog on the card seemed pleased with its new address.

Mira joined Frog’s lively rhythm while Ada watched from the porch, and the invitation stayed safely with its new owner. The still pond carried the music in bright circles; even the lily pad seemed to bounce, as if it had swallowed a very polite trampoline.

title: The Pond Concert Promise

Ada looked at the waving reeds and nodded. “Then we’ll give my lily pad something sturdy to hold.”

Ada and Ben anchored the lily pad against the breeze. Ben held the cord while Ada pressed the anchor down; the pad stopped drifting and stayed put.

With the lily pad anchored against the breeze, Frog turned it into a lively rhythm. His drumbeat and the pad’s gentle thump made a bouncy, dependable pulse.

Ada picked up the painted invitation and carried it from the garden to the porch. She held it carefully; the blue frog on its front had very important-looking spots.

With the invitation waiting on the porch, Ada walked up from the garden. She practiced her polite knock, then decided one knock was plenty.

Mira joined the lively pond rhythm from the porch, tapping along with her fingers. Her smile arrived on the beat, though her left thumb was slightly ahead of everyone.

Ada gave Mira the painted invitation. “You’re invited to join Frog’s concert,” Ada said. Mira accepted the card, already listening for the next beat.

The invitation was safely delivered: Mira now owned the painted card, and Ada’s delivery was complete. The blue frog on the card seemed pleased with its new address.

Mira joined the lively rhythm as Frog played his anchored lily-pad beat. The breeze whisked over the water, but the pad stayed steady, and Ada’s invitation remained safely with Mira. Sunlight flashed on the ripples while Ben grinned beside the anchor, right on the beat.

title: The Pond Concert Promise
story:
Ada wanted to invite Mira to Frog’s pond concert, and Ben wanted to help. Yet Mira wanted quiet while a breeze skimmed the pond, and Ada’s wide lily pad still waited in the garden. Frog’s acorn drum waited too, although it belonged to Frog and not to Ada.

Frog noticed a breeze ruffling the pond. “The water is tickling the reeds,” he said. “A lily pad might go sailing without buying a ticket.”

Ada picked up the painted invitation and carried it from the garden to the porch. She held it carefully; the blue frog on its front had very important-looking spots.

Frog told Ada about the breezy pond. Ada looked at the waving reeds and nodded. “Then we’ll give my lily pad something sturdy to hold.” Frog carried his acorn drum from the garden to the pond. He set it near the water, where its round wooden belly was ready to go bonk—or perhaps merely bonk politely. Ada pushed her wide lily pad from the garden onto the pond. It floated broad and steady, making a perfect little platform for Frog’s planned rhythm.

Ada and Ben anchored the lily pad against the breeze. Ben held the cord while Ada pressed the anchor down; the pad stopped drifting and stayed put.

Ada peeked toward Mira’s porch and noticed Mira sitting with a book, enjoying quiet. “Quiet,” Ada whispered, “is Mira’s wish today.”

With the invitation waiting on the porch, Ada walked up from the garden. She practiced her polite knock, then decided one knock was plenty.

Ada told Frog, “Mira wants quiet today.” Frog nodded. “Then my drum shall use its teeny-tiniest toes.”

Knowing Mira wanted quiet, Frog played a gentle song on the acorn drum. Tap, hush, tap—each note skimmed the pond like a tiny pebble that had learned manners.

Mira smiled and listened to Frog’s gentle pond song. She stayed on the porch, quiet as a sleeping feather, while the soft taps reached her.

Ada gave Mira the painted invitation. “A pond concert,” she said, “with a very small volume knob.” Mira accepted it from Ada with a curious smile.

The invitation was safely delivered: Mira now owned the painted card, and Ada’s delivery was complete. The blue frog on the card seemed pleased with its new address.

Mira smiled and listened to Frog’s gentle song while the anchored lily pad held steady in the breezy pond. Ben’s helping hands had made a difference, and Ada’s invitation rested with Mira. Across the water, soft notes trembled like tiny lanterns tied safely to their strings.

title: The Pond Concert Promise
story:
Ada planned to invite Mira to Frog’s pond concert, while Ben hoped to help. Mira wanted to join, but the pond was perfectly still and the concert tools were scattered in the garden. Ada’s painted invitation waited beside a wide lily pad, as if both were awaiting instructions.

Ada watched Mira on the porch, where Mira leaned forward as though eager for music. “She wants to join,” Ada observed. “That is wonderfully less quiet than a potato.” Ada pushed her wide lily pad from the garden onto the pond. It floated broad and steady, making a perfect little platform for Frog’s planned rhythm.

Ada picked up the painted invitation and carried it from the garden to the porch. She held it carefully; the blue frog on its front had very important-looking spots.

Ada told Frog that Mira wanted to join the concert. Frog puffed up happily. “Excellent! I know three rhythms and one accidental sneeze.”

Frog began a lively rhythm on the lily pad. The still pond let every plip and plop travel outward, while the pad bobbed like a cheerful green drumhead.

Mira joined the lively pond rhythm from the porch, tapping along with her fingers. Her smile arrived on the beat, though her left thumb was slightly ahead of everyone.

With the invitation waiting on the porch, Ada walked up from the garden. She practiced her polite knock, then decided one knock was plenty.

Ada gave Mira the painted invitation. “You’re invited to join Frog’s concert,” Ada said. Mira accepted the card, already listening for the next beat.

The invitation was safely delivered: Mira now owned the painted card, and Ada’s delivery was complete. The blue frog on the card seemed pleased with its new address.

Mira joined Frog’s lively rhythm while Ada watched from the porch, and the invitation stayed safely with its new owner. The still pond carried the music in bright circles; even the lily pad seemed to bounce, as if it had swallowed a very polite trampoline.

title: The Pond Concert Promise
story:
Ada hoped to invite Mira to Frog’s pond concert, and Ben hoped to help. Mira wanted to join, but a breeze teased the pond and the wide lily pad was still in the garden. Frog’s drum waited there too, stubbornly refusing to teleport.

Frog noticed a breeze ruffling the pond. “The water is tickling the reeds,” he said. “A lily pad might go sailing without buying a ticket.”

Ada picked up the painted invitation and carried it from the garden to the porch. She held it carefully; the blue frog on its front had very important-looking spots.

Ada watched Mira on the porch, where Mira leaned forward as though eager for music. “She wants to join,” Ada observed. “That is wonderfully less quiet than a potato.” Ada pushed her wide lily pad from the garden onto the pond. It floated broad and steady, making a perfect little platform for Frog’s planned rhythm. Frog told Ada about the breezy pond. Ada looked at the waving reeds and nodded. “Then we’ll give my lily pad something sturdy to hold.”

Ada and Ben anchored the lily pad against the breeze. Ben held the cord while Ada pressed the anchor down; the pad stopped drifting and stayed put.

Ada told Frog that Mira wanted to join the concert. Frog puffed up happily. “Excellent! I know three rhythms and one accidental sneeze.”

With the invitation waiting on the porch, Ada walked up from the garden. She practiced her polite knock, then decided one knock was plenty.

Ada gave Mira the painted invitation. “You’re invited to join Frog’s concert,” Ada said. Mira accepted the card, already listening for the next beat.

With the lily pad anchored against the breeze, Frog turned it into a lively rhythm. His drumbeat and the pad’s gentle thump made a bouncy, dependable pulse.

Mira joined the lively pond rhythm from the porch, tapping along with her fingers. Her smile arrived on the beat, though her left thumb was slightly ahead of everyone.

The invitation was safely delivered: Mira now owned the painted card, and Ada’s delivery was complete. The blue frog on the card seemed pleased with its new address.

Mira joined the lively rhythm as Frog played his anchored lily-pad beat. The breeze whisked over the water, but the pad stayed steady, and Ada’s invitation remained safely with Mira. Sunlight flashed on the ripples while Ben grinned beside the anchor, right on the beat.

title: The Pond Concert Promise
story:
Ada hoped to invite Mira to Frog’s pond concert, and Ben hoped to help. Mira wanted to join, but a breeze teased the pond and the wide lily pad was still in the garden. Frog’s drum waited there too, stubbornly refusing to teleport.

Ada picked up the painted invitation and carried it from the garden to the porch. She held it carefully; the blue frog on its front had very important-looking spots.

Ada pushed her wide lily pad from the garden onto the pond. It floated broad and steady, making a perfect little platform for Frog’s planned rhythm.

With the invitation waiting on the porch, Ada walked up from the garden. She practiced her polite knock, then decided one knock was plenty.

Ada watched Mira on the porch, where Mira leaned forward as though eager for music. “She wants to join,” Ada observed. “That is wonderfully less quiet than a potato.” Frog noticed a breeze ruffling the pond. “The water is tickling the reeds,” he said. “A lily pad might go sailing without buying a ticket.” Frog told Ada about the breezy pond. Ada looked at the waving reeds and nodded. “Then we’ll give my lily pad something sturdy to hold.” Ada told Frog that Mira wanted to join the concert. Frog puffed up happily. “Excellent! I know three rhythms and one accidental sneeze.”

Ada gave Mira the painted invitation. “You’re invited to join Frog’s concert,” Ada said. Mira accepted the card, already listening for the next beat.

Ada and Ben anchored the lily pad against the breeze. Ben held the cord while Ada pressed the anchor down; the pad stopped drifting and stayed put.

With the lily pad anchored against the breeze, Frog turned it into a lively rhythm. His drumbeat and the pad’s gentle thump made a bouncy, dependable pulse.

The invitation was safely delivered: Mira now owned the painted card, and Ada’s delivery was complete. The blue frog on the card seemed pleased with its new address.

Mira joined the lively pond rhythm from the porch, tapping along with her fingers. Her smile arrived on the beat, though her left thumb was slightly ahead of everyone.

Mira joined the lively rhythm as Frog played his anchored lily-pad beat. The breeze whisked over the water, but the pad stayed steady, and Ada’s invitation remained safely with Mira. Sunlight flashed on the ripples while Ben grinned beside the anchor, right on the beat.

title: The Pond Concert Promise
story:
Ada planned to invite Mira to Frog’s pond concert, while Ben hoped to help. Mira wanted to join, but the pond was perfectly still and the concert tools were scattered in the garden. Ada’s painted invitation waited beside a wide lily pad, as if both were awaiting instructions.

Ada pushed her wide lily pad from the garden onto the pond. It floated broad and steady, making a perfect little platform for Frog’s planned rhythm. Ada watched Mira on the porch, where Mira leaned forward as though eager for music. “She wants to join,” Ada observed. “That is wonderfully less quiet than a potato.” Ada told Frog that Mira wanted to join the concert. Frog puffed up happily. “Excellent! I know three rhythms and one accidental sneeze.”

Ada picked up the painted invitation and carried it from the garden to the porch. She held it carefully; the blue frog on its front had very important-looking spots.

Frog began a lively rhythm on the lily pad. The still pond let every plip and plop travel outward, while the pad bobbed like a cheerful green drumhead.

With the invitation waiting on the porch, Ada walked up from the garden. She practiced her polite knock, then decided one knock was plenty.

Ada gave Mira the painted invitation. “You’re invited to join Frog’s concert,” Ada said. Mira accepted the card, already listening for the next beat.

The invitation was safely delivered: Mira now owned the painted card, and Ada’s delivery was complete. The blue frog on the card seemed pleased with its new address.

Mira joined the lively pond rhythm from the porch, tapping along with her fingers. Her smile arrived on the beat, though her left thumb was slightly ahead of everyone.

Mira joined Frog’s lively rhythm while Ada watched from the porch, and the invitation stayed safely with its new owner. The still pond carried the music in bright circles; even the lily pad seemed to bounce, as if it had swallowed a very polite trampoline.

title: The Pond Concert Promise
story:
Ada wanted to invite Mira to Frog’s pond concert, and Ben wanted to help. Yet Mira wanted quiet while a breeze skimmed the pond, and Ada’s wide lily pad still waited in the garden. Frog’s acorn drum waited too, although it belonged to Frog and not to Ada.

Ada pushed her wide lily pad from the garden onto the pond. It floated broad and steady, making a perfect little platform for Frog’s planned rhythm. Frog noticed a breeze ruffling the pond. “The water is tickling the reeds,” he said. “A lily pad might go sailing without buying a ticket.” Frog carried his acorn drum from the garden to the pond. He set it near the water, where its round wooden belly was ready to go bonk—or perhaps merely bonk politely.

Ada picked up the painted invitation and carried it from the garden to the porch. She held it carefully; the blue frog on its front had very important-looking spots.

With the invitation waiting on the porch, Ada walked up from the garden. She practiced her polite knock, then decided one knock was plenty.

Ada peeked toward Mira’s porch and noticed Mira sitting with a book, enjoying quiet. “Quiet,” Ada whispered, “is Mira’s wish today.” Frog told Ada about the breezy pond. Ada looked at the waving reeds and nodded. “Then we’ll give my lily pad something sturdy to hold.” Ada told Frog, “Mira wants quiet today.” Frog nodded. “Then my drum shall use its teeny-tiniest toes.”

Ada gave Mira the painted invitation. “A pond concert,” she said, “with a very small volume knob.” Mira accepted it from Ada with a curious smile.

Ada and Ben anchored the lily pad against the breeze. Ben held the cord while Ada pressed the anchor down; the pad stopped drifting and stayed put.

The invitation was safely delivered: Mira now owned the painted card, and Ada’s delivery was complete. The blue frog on the card seemed pleased with its new address.

Knowing Mira wanted quiet, Frog played a gentle song on the acorn drum. Tap, hush, tap—each note skimmed the pond like a tiny pebble that had learned manners.

Mira smiled and listened to Frog’s gentle pond song. She stayed on the porch, quiet as a sleeping feather, while the soft taps reached her.

Mira smiled and listened to Frog’s gentle song while the anchored lily pad held steady in the breezy pond. Ben’s helping hands had made a difference, and Ada’s invitation rested with Mira. Across the water, soft notes trembled like tiny lanterns tied safely to their strings.

title: The Pond Concert Promise
story:
Ada hoped to invite Mira to Frog’s pond concert, and Ben hoped to help. Mira wanted to join, but a breeze teased the pond and the wide lily pad was still in the garden. Frog’s drum waited there too, stubbornly refusing to teleport.

Ada watched Mira on the porch, where Mira leaned forward as though eager for music. “She wants to join,” Ada observed. “That is wonderfully less quiet than a potato.” Frog noticed a breeze ruffling the pond. “The water is tickling the reeds,” he said. “A lily pad might go sailing without buying a ticket.” Ada told Frog that Mira wanted to join the concert. Frog puffed up happily. “Excellent! I know three rhythms and one accidental sneeze.”

Ada picked up the painted invitation and carried it from the garden to the porch. She held it carefully; the blue frog on its front had very important-looking spots.

Ada pushed her wide lily pad from the garden onto the pond. It floated broad and steady, making a perfect little platform for Frog’s planned rhythm. Frog told Ada about the breezy pond. Ada looked at the waving reeds and nodded. “Then we’ll give my lily pad something sturdy to hold.”

With the invitation waiting on the porch, Ada walked up from the garden. She practiced her polite knock, then decided one knock was plenty.

Ada and Ben anchored the lily pad against the breeze. Ben held the cord while Ada pressed the anchor down; the pad stopped drifting and stayed put.

With the lily pad anchored against the breeze, Frog turned it into a lively rhythm. His drumbeat and the pad’s gentle thump made a bouncy, dependable pulse.

Ada gave Mira the painted invitation. “You’re invited to join Frog’s concert,” Ada said. Mira accepted the card, already listening for the next beat.

Mira joined the lively pond rhythm from the porch, tapping along with her fingers. Her smile arrived on the beat, though her left thumb was slightly ahead of everyone.

The invitation was safely delivered: Mira now owned the painted card, and Ada’s delivery was complete. The blue frog on the card seemed pleased with its new address.

Mira joined the lively rhythm as Frog played his anchored lily-pad beat. The breeze whisked over the water, but the pad stayed steady, and Ada’s invitation remained safely with Mira. Sunlight flashed on the ripples while Ben grinned beside the anchor, right on the beat.

title: The Pond Concert Promise
story:
Ada wanted to invite Mira to Frog’s pond concert, and Ben wanted to help. Yet Mira wanted quiet while a breeze skimmed the pond, and Ada’s wide lily pad still waited in the garden. Frog’s acorn drum waited too, although it belonged to Frog and not to Ada.

Frog carried his acorn drum from the garden to the pond. He set it near the water, where its round wooden belly was ready to go bonk—or perhaps merely bonk politely. Ada peeked toward Mira’s porch and noticed Mira sitting with a book, enjoying quiet. “Quiet,” Ada whispered, “is Mira’s wish today.”

Ada picked up the painted invitation and carried it from the garden to the porch. She held it carefully; the blue frog on its front had very important-looking spots.

With the invitation waiting on the porch, Ada walked up from the garden. She practiced her polite knock, then decided one knock was plenty.

Ada gave Mira the painted invitation. “A pond concert,” she said, “with a very small volume knob.” Mira accepted it from Ada with a curious smile.

The invitation was safely delivered: Mira now owned the painted card, and Ada’s delivery was complete. The blue frog on the card seemed pleased with its new address.

Ada told Frog, “Mira wants quiet today.” Frog nodded. “Then my drum shall use its teeny-tiniest toes.”

Knowing Mira wanted quiet, Frog played a gentle song on the acorn drum. Tap, hush, tap—each note skimmed the pond like a tiny pebble that had learned manners.

Mira smiled and listened to Frog’s gentle pond song. She stayed on the porch, quiet as a sleeping feather, while the soft taps reached her.

Mira smiled and listened as Frog’s gentle notes floated across the still pond. Ada’s invitation rested safely in Mira’s hands, and the acorn drum made no thunder at all. In the evening light, each quiet ripple looked like a little silver ear, listening too.

title: The Pond Concert Promise
story:
Ada hoped to invite Mira to Frog’s pond concert, and Ben hoped to help. Mira wanted to join, but a breeze teased the pond and the wide lily pad was still in the garden. Frog’s drum waited there too, stubbornly refusing to teleport.

Ada pushed her wide lily pad from the garden onto the pond. It floated broad and steady, making a perfect little platform for Frog’s planned rhythm.

Ada picked up the painted invitation and carried it from the garden to the porch. She held it carefully; the blue frog on its front had very important-looking spots.

With the invitation waiting on the porch, Ada walked up from the garden. She practiced her polite knock, then decided one knock was plenty.

Frog noticed a breeze ruffling the pond. “The water is tickling the reeds,” he said. “A lily pad might go sailing without buying a ticket.” Frog told Ada about the breezy pond. Ada looked at the waving reeds and nodded. “Then we’ll give my lily pad something sturdy to hold.” Ada watched Mira on the porch, where Mira leaned forward as though eager for music. “She wants to join,” Ada observed. “That is wonderfully less quiet than a potato.”

Ada gave Mira the painted invitation. “You’re invited to join Frog’s concert,” Ada said. Mira accepted the card, already listening for the next beat.

Ada told Frog that Mira wanted to join the concert. Frog puffed up happily. “Excellent! I know three rhythms and one accidental sneeze.”

Ada and Ben anchored the lily pad against the breeze. Ben held the cord while Ada pressed the anchor down; the pad stopped drifting and stayed put.

The invitation was safely delivered: Mira now owned the painted card, and Ada’s delivery was complete. The blue frog on the card seemed pleased with its new address.

With the lily pad anchored against the breeze, Frog turned it into a lively rhythm. His drumbeat and the pad’s gentle thump made a bouncy, dependable pulse.

Mira joined the lively pond rhythm from the porch, tapping along with her fingers. Her smile arrived on the beat, though her left thumb was slightly ahead of everyone.

Mira joined the lively rhythm as Frog played his anchored lily-pad beat. The breeze whisked over the water, but the pad stayed steady, and Ada’s invitation remained safely with Mira. Sunlight flashed on the ripples while Ben grinned beside the anchor, right on the beat.

title: The Pond Concert Promise
story:
Ada wanted to invite Mira to Frog’s pond concert, and Ben wanted to help. But the pond was still, Mira wanted quiet, and nobody yet knew what sort of concert would fit. The painted invitation waited in Ada’s garden beside Frog’s drum.

Frog carried his acorn drum from the garden to the pond. He set it near the water, where its round wooden belly was ready to go bonk—or perhaps merely bonk politely. Ada peeked toward Mira’s porch and noticed Mira sitting with a book, enjoying quiet. “Quiet,” Ada whispered, “is Mira’s wish today.” Ada told Frog, “Mira wants quiet today.” Frog nodded. “Then my drum shall use its teeny-tiniest toes.”

Knowing Mira wanted quiet, Frog played a gentle song on the acorn drum. Tap, hush, tap—each note skimmed the pond like a tiny pebble that had learned manners.

Ada picked up the painted invitation and carried it from the garden to the porch. She held it carefully; the blue frog on its front had very important-looking spots.

With the invitation waiting on the porch, Ada walked up from the garden. She practiced her polite knock, then decided one knock was plenty.

Mira smiled and listened to Frog’s gentle pond song. She stayed on the porch, quiet as a sleeping feather, while the soft taps reached her.

Ada gave Mira the painted invitation. “A pond concert,” she said, “with a very small volume knob.” Mira accepted it from Ada with a curious smile.

The invitation was safely delivered: Mira now owned the painted card, and Ada’s delivery was complete. The blue frog on the card seemed pleased with its new address.

Mira smiled and listened as Frog’s gentle notes floated across the still pond. Ada’s invitation rested safely in Mira’s hands, and the acorn drum made no thunder at all. In the evening light, each quiet ripple looked like a little silver ear, listening too.

Ada picked up the painted invitation and carried it from the garden to the porch. She held it carefully; the blue frog on its front had very important-looking spots.

Ada pushed her wide lily pad from the garden onto the pond. It floated broad and steady, making a perfect little platform for Frog’s planned rhythm. Ada peeked toward Mira’s porch and noticed Mira sitting with a book, enjoying quiet. “Quiet,” Ada whispered, “is Mira’s wish today.”
With the invitation waiting on the porch, Ada walked up from the garden. She practiced her polite knock, then decided one knock was plenty.

Frog noticed a breeze ruffling the pond. “The water is tickling the reeds,” he said. “A lily pad might go sailing without buying a ticket.” Frog told Ada about the breezy pond. Ada looked at the waving reeds and nodded. “Then we’ll give my lily pad something sturdy to hold.”
Ada gave Mira the painted invitation. “A pond concert,” she said, “with a very small volume knob.” Mira accepted it from Ada with a curious smile.
Ada told Frog, “Mira wants quiet today.” Frog nodded. “Then my drum shall use its teeny-tiniest toes.”
Ada and Ben anchored the lily pad against the breeze. Ben held the cord while Ada pressed the anchor down; the pad stopped drifting and stayed put.
